F001.note: Timeout-with-work is preserved and the canonical strictly-shrinking 3->1 case is fixed, but no_progress still trips on verdict equality whenever the signature count is not strictly smaller; it does not implement the required identical-signature-set condition. diminishing_returns also only exempts strictly decreasing counts, not all changed finding sets.

F002.note: _latest_auditor_envelope now ranks auditor envelopes by mtime with iteration as a tie-break, which fixes fresh low-index signed_off versus stale high-index needs_changes while preserving single-envelope and monotonic-run behavior.

F003.note: The wired 3->1->0 convergence demonstration is useful, but the regression tests encode the wrong no_progress expectation for changed flat findings and do not prove the stated acceptance criteria.

findings.issue: check_no_progress still uses same-verdict equality as the trip condition after only a strictly-shrinking count carve-out. Changed same-count envelopes such as {A}->{B}, and growing envelopes such as {A}->{A,B}, still trip stopped_no_progress even though F001 requires tripping only when the auditor finding-signature SET is identical across consecutive needs_changes rounds.

check_diminishing_returns only treats strictly decreasing signature counts as progress. Changed sets with a persisted finding but flat count, e.g. {A,B}->{A,C}, still trip via intersection even though the acceptance language says shrinking/changing blocking finding sets should be treated as progress.

The tests contradict the contract: test_no_progress_envelope_flat_count_still_trips and the flat-distinct wired test expect changed findings with unchanged needs_changes verdict to stop at round 2. The growing test also only asserts not signed_off, so it does not prove the claimed breaker behavior or precedence.
